title: LeanTeX, explained
h1: LeanTeX: writing Beamer slide decks in Lean 4
lead: LeanTeX is Kiran Gopinathan's Lean 4 library for writing LaTeX Beamer presentations as Lean code: slides are Lean definitions, a LaTeX-like DSL and a raw latex![| … |] literal build them, and lake exec GenerateSlides turns them into a PDF. It is a tool, not a proof development: it contains no theorems at all, so this site explains what its parsers, elaborators and code generator do rather than what they prove.
desc: An unofficial plain-English tour of LeanTeX, Kiran Gopinathan's Lean 4 metaprogramming library that turns Lean definitions into Beamer slides: the raw-LaTeX literal, the slide and TikZ DSLs, the compile-time registries, and the PDF build.
startNote: LeanTeX has no theorems, so the "headlines" here are its main pieces of machinery. Start with the latex![| … |] literal, then the slide DSL and the TikZ DSL. To see how a deck becomes a PDF, read #leantex_config and generateSlides, and the bootstrap for what lake exec GenerateSlides does to your project. The review page lists a few suspected bugs found by reading.
sizeNote: About 1,040 lines of Lean in 11 files, plus a 130-line example project. No theorems.
agentCtx: LeanTeX: a Lean 4 metaprogramming library (custom parser, syntax categories, elaborators, environment extensions) that generates LaTeX Beamer slides from Lean definitions and runs pdflatex. No theorems.

gloss.String: Text. Almost everything LeanTeX builds is ultimately a string of LaTeX.
gloss.List: A finite list: of slides, of slide contents, of options.
gloss.Option: Either some x or none; used for optional titles, names and positions.
gloss.Nat: The natural numbers 0, 1, 2, …; here, Beamer overlay step numbers.
gloss.IO: Lean's type of programs with side effects (files, processes). generateSlides is one.
gloss.MetaM: Lean's metaprogramming monad: code that runs inside Lean while it reads a file and can inspect or change the environment.
gloss.TermElabM: The monad of Lean's term elaborator, which turns syntax into typed expressions.
gloss.MacroM: The monad of Lean macros: code that rewrites syntax into other syntax.
gloss.CommandElab: A handler for a top-level command such as #leantex_config.
gloss.ParserFn: A low-level Lean parser function: it reads characters and builds syntax.
gloss.Syntax: Lean's representation of parsed source code, before elaboration.
gloss.TSyntax: Syntax tagged with the grammar category it belongs to.
gloss.Std.HashMap: A hash map from keys to values; iteration order is not insertion order.
